location.basis: Published position of the Valamio Timbo mound, 23 deg 14 min 15 s N, 70 deg 40 min 39 s E (Wikipedia and the Shikarpur lithic-assemblage paper in Journal of Lithic Studies), which falls on an oval wooded mound of about 190 x 220 m south of National Highway 41 and east of a reservoir. We take this mound to be the site.

sources.citation_or_service: Esri World Imagery tile service, https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}; Source: Esri, Vantor, Earthstar Geographics, and the GIS User Community. Imagery under the measured structures (World_Imagery/MapServer identify): Vantor Vivid (LG01), source resolution 0.34 m, deepest real zoom 18.
sources.north_label_text: no label; Web Mercator (EPSG:3857) tile grid, whose columns run to true north

main_system_reason: No system: we found no measurable Harappan line.
notes: The Esri imagery is a Vantor Vivid mosaic of 20 March 2026 with real detail to zoom 18 (0.55 m per pixel). The mound is covered by a dense thicket (probably Prosopis) with a network of small clearings; neither the fortification wall nor the eastern gate exposed by the excavations of 1987-90 and 2007-2014 is visible through it. The straight lines nearby are the highway, a railway, field edges and the fence of an electrical substation. Shikarpur is not measurable from this imagery.
